name: Dapsone gel (Aczone)

lead: Dapsone gel (Aczone) is a prescription topical for acne. It has been studied in large registered trials, including in children and people with skin of color.
It is available in 5% and 7.5% strengths.

paras: Dapsone inhibits bacterial folate synthesis and has anti-inflammatory activity through myeloperoxidase inhibition.
Mild irritation, dryness, redness; temporary yellow-orange discoloration with benzoyl peroxide. Prescription-only.

lead: Dapsone gel, sold as Aczone, is a prescription topical gel for acne vulgaris. Wikipedia reports that QLT USA developed the 5% gel in the early 2000s and that the FDA approved a 7.5% gel in February 2016 [1].

Dapsone has both antibacterial and anti-inflammatory actions, and Wikipedia reports that the 5% gel did not cause clinically significant hemoglobin declines in people with G6PD deficiency [1]. Many registered trials have studied the gel, including two phase 3 studies enrolling over 2,000 patients each [2][3].

paras: The gel treats acne vulgaris. Registered trials covered children aged 9 to 11 [4], women with skin of color [5], truncal acne [6], and maintenance after oral doxycycline [7]. A terminated trial tested 5% gel in dermatitis herpetiformis [8].

Mild irritation, redness, dryness, burning and itching can occur. Use with benzoyl peroxide can cause temporary yellow or orange skin discoloration. Methemoglobinemia is linked in the source to long-term oral dapsone, not the topical gel [1].

As an antibacterial, dapsone inhibits bacterial folate synthesis; as an anti-inflammatory, it inhibits myeloperoxidase [1]. Because it is poorly soluble in water, early topical formulations were hard to develop [1].

Two phase 3 trials of dapsone gel in acne enrolled 2,238 and 2,102 patients [2][3]. A phase 1 study compared a test product with Aczone 5% and placebo (n=1134) [9]. A phase 4 trial compared 7.5% gel with 20% trichloroacetic acid [10]. Detailed results are not summarised here.
Dapsone was first synthesised in 1908, studied as an antibiotic in 1937 and used for leprosy from 1945 [1].

timeline.event: Dapsone first studied as an antibiotic [1].
